newsitem.title: GERMANY: German metal workers say regional wage talks fail.
newsitem.headline: German metal workers say regional wage talks fail.

text.p: German metal workers union IG Metall said on Tuesday that regional wage talks in North Rhine-Westphalia, which had been seen to be the key to a possible national deal, had collapsed.
"The talks have collapsed," union negotiator Harald Schartau told journalists after all-night discussions, adding this had likely been the last chance to hammer out a deal at the negotiating table.

Talks in the region, which is home to some of Germany's largest steel producers and 850,000 workers in the sector, began on Monday morning and were seen to possibly provide a pilot agreement for the industry as a whole after attempts to secure a nationwide deal failed last month.

Martin Kannegiesser, head negotiator for the employers, said the two sides had agreed on many issues, but disagreements about a new model which sought to link special payments to sickdays had caused the talks to collapse.
"Both sides had erected many barriers, we tried to do a slalom, but we fell down," he told journalists.

Earlier in the marathon talks, officials from both sides had been optimistic a compromise could be worked out on issues including wages, job security and holiday pay. The main sticking point was expected to be sick pay entitlements, which employers are seeking to cut to 80 percent in accordance with a new law that came into effect in October.
The union had said it must stick with 100 percent sick pay.
Some commentators had already been sceptical that a regional agreement could be reached after an attempt to find points of agreement on sick pay failed in the south-west state of Baden-Wuerttemberg.

On Monday, the union had said that if these wage talks as well as the normal wage round in January failed, then a strike ballot would be called by the end of February. "Then I am sure we would end up striking," Walter Riester, deputy chairman of IG Metall told German radio on Monday. -- Svea Herbst-Bayliss, Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525
